owner_intent: When a Patch Pack or Task Pack is registered, Mechanicus must inspect the task demand and propose the required languages, tools, validators and missing capabilities.
Mechanicus must mathematically evaluate tool combinations for cheaper, cleaner and more reliable execution.
Mechanicus must understand the heart-of-machine layer: tools, languages, libraries, engines, validators and runtime hosts required for blood to flow through Imperium.
Mechanicus recommendation is advisory until Owner/Throne policy makes a lane blocking.
Mechanicus must report unknown or missing capabilities instead of pretending the system can do the task.
Mechanicus should prefer existing admitted tools over creating new tools, unless gaps make a new tool necessary.
core_laws: A task is not registered as machine-ready until Mechanicus can name the required tool stack or declare missing capability.
Tool choice must be scored, not guessed.
Cheapest is not best if cleanliness or reliability collapses.
Cleanest is not best if no toolchain exists.
Reliable is not best if it creates monolith or blocks Owner workflow.
Unknown demand must become an Owner-visible capability gap.
Tool composition plans do not execute the task.
Tool composition plans do not install packages.
Tool composition plans do not claim runtime proof.
